subject.title: fix(plugins): resolve openclaw/plugin-sdk/<subpath> imports without root-alias.cjs fall-through (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw's native plugin loader ever expose built `dist/plugin-sdk/*.js` artifacts that are absent from the canonical package export and SDK entrypoint inventory?
rationale: That choice defines a compatibility and security boundary for every native plugin and cannot be inferred safely from tests alone; current docs and mainline guardrails favor an explicit export-driven contract.

options.title: Keep aliases export-driven
options.body: Remove generic artifact backfill and add only intentional public or owner-reserved subpaths through the canonical export and entrypoint contract.

options.title: Approve artifact backfill
options.body: Accept the parallel loader-only surface only with explicit approval, documented semantics, deny-by-default gating, package-parity tests, and real installed-runtime proof.

options.title: Close as overtaken
options.body: Close this branch if current main's supported subpath export and external native-plugin resolution already cover the intended harness startup case.

recommendation.title: Keep aliases export-driven
recommendation.body: Remove generic artifact backfill and add only intentional public or owner-reserved subpaths through the canonical export and entrypoint contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work owns the external-plugin SDK alias resolution path and release export guard involved in this decision.
